historyTimeline.h2: Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 1.5 dCi variant launched, it served as the highly economical, long-distance diesel workhorse of the Nissan Micra range, introducing the renowned Renault-sourced K9K engine to the K12 generation and continuing into the K13 with improved emissions compliance.

milestones.description: K9K introduced in the K12 facelift, 1.5L dCi, 65-86 PS, offering strong fuel economy and high torque for high-mileage drivers.
K13 generation launched, retaining the K9K 1.5 dCi with updated engine management, improved DPF integration, and Euro 5 compliance.
Production of the 1.5 dCi ended in the UK as the K15 generation shifted exclusively to turbocharged petrol and mild-hybrid powertrains.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: Diesel Injector Failure & EGR Clogging - Why the Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi (K9K) Loses Performance
problems.rootCause: High-pressure diesel injectors wear internally, causing poor atomisation, black smoke, and rough running. Combined with EGR clogging from urban driving, this strains the engine and can lead to DPF blockages.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, fit reconditioned units, code to ECU, clean EGR
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine block and turbo are healthy; requires specialist diagnostics

items.question: What are the signs of injector or turbo failure in a Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi?
items.answer: Injector or turbo failure in the Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi usually presents as black or blue smoke from the exhaust, rough idling, and a noticeable loss of power.
keyPoints: You may notice increased oil consumption or a knocking sound from the engine bay.
The vehicle may enter limp mode to protect the engine from further damage.
Ignoring these signs can lead to catastrophic internal engine failure.

items.answer: For a Nissan Micra 1.5 dCi (2007-2017) valued between £1,500 and £5,000, a full rebuilt engine must be evaluated carefully against the vehicle's age.
keyPoints: If the vehicle is in excellent cosmetic and mechanical condition otherwise, a reconditioned engine with a 12-month warranty is a sound investment.
For lower-value examples, a quality used engine or targeted repair (like injector replacement) is often the most financially sensible route.
Always evaluate scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full rebuild.
